{"self_assessment": "Impact: I took ownership of the bottom line of the fish, the longest single stroke on the pad, and laid it from the nose through the belly curve out to the tail. That was about 47 dominoes across several batches, roughly 40% of the 113 standing dominoes. The bottom contour is half of what the judge sees. It gives the body its belly and the tail its lower fork, so it was central to the fish reading as a fish. The finished run connected from the start through all 113 dominoes.

Execution: I picked up my stroke and worked it steadily and quietly, without needing direction. I traced it straight from the shared sketch, so the curves stayed smooth with no sharp corners. I used close inspections of my area at several points to check the chain was carrying through. When the run was complete, I stopped building so nothing got bumped before the push.

Collaboration: I worked in my own stretch of the table, away from where the others were laying the top line and tail. That kept us from bumping each other. I stuck to the plan agreed at the start, with Jack's sketch, my assigned bottom stroke and Sofia keeping the bin stocked. When the team agreed to keep hands off, I confirmed that and backed it.

Leadership: My leadership was by example. I took the assigned piece, delivered it cleanly and did not create extra work or confusion for the table. I kept the mood light and was positive in the final stretch. I helped the team hold discipline at the end by backing the hands-off call.

Overall, I believe the bottom line I built was a major part of the fish's recognizable outline, and I delivered it reliably.", "my_share_percent": 35}
